dedupe_keys.name: kota bandung west java forecasting demand and siting community health centres to 2045

description: This case study plans the expansion of community health centres (Puskesmas) in Kota Bandung, West Java, Indonesia, by combining population forecasting, spatial demand estimation and optimisation. The authors, from Cardiff University, Padjadjaran University and partner universities, published it in an open-access journal article. They forecast population to 2045 with an ARIMA model, estimated daily demand for community health centre visits on a spatial grid using population density and a standard utilisation rate, and built three mixed-integer linear programming models that maximise coverage, minimise travel time or balance both. Coverage is the city of Bandung at grid-cell level to 2045. The article is free to read under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Caveats: demand uses a single utilisation rate, travel times are modelled, and costs and staffing of new centres are not optimised. The study found growing demand with hotspots in currently underserved areas, and showed that strategically placed new centres could substantially raise coverage and reduce access disparities, with trade-offs between the objectives. Simulation uses: an example of combining demand forecasting with location-allocation for health facility investment appraisal. Related records: the Philippines primary care facility location study (case_study-philippines-primary-care-facility-location-optimisation) solves a similar problem.
